summary: Completed targeted agent, connector and event reliability review at cb438d1083e9ae3e2a38dd8e5d7dba4c778b2e89. One medium recovery defect was reproduced: temporary connector overload removes that connector from subsequent agent attempts until a person retries it. No supported high or critical finding was identified within this scope.
coverage: Agent model boundary: packages/agents/src/{host,runtime,claude,mode,tools,agents}.ts; examined tool allowlists and schema validation, bounded model turns, signal forwarding, licensed task/corpus/evidence-title filtering, proposal-only mutation, recorded-check provenance, and selected offline evidence-renewal paths. Inspected policy template generation and related licensing, evidence-provenance and corpus-claims test source.

Run lifecycle: apps/server/src/services/run-execution.ts and visua.ts run queue admission, claims, epoch/lease ownership, heartbeats, cancellation, expired-owner interruption, recorder queues, snapshot refresh, connector persistence and graceful stop; inspected run-reliability and two-instance-automation test source.

Approval boundary: apps/server/src/services/{proposal-validation,proposal-review}.ts and visua.ts proposal creation, validation, savepoint preview/rollback, review tokens, batch conflict handling, immutable source-check filing, evidence review preconditions and autonomy allowlist; inspected proposal-validation and proposal-review test source and HTTP approval token enforcement in app.ts.

Connectors: apps/server/src/connectors/{index,limits,network,web-posture,repo-scan}.ts plus auth/egress.ts and work-scope.ts; traced public-only socket DNS, mixed-address rejection, redirect and downgrade checks, response/body limits, cancellation versus physical DNS lifetime, global concurrency and approved repository roots/no-follow reads. Inspected connector-boundaries and connector-dns-lifetime test source.

Events: apps/server/src/{bus,workspace-events}.ts, storage/events.ts, and apps/web/src/lib/events.ts; traced post-commit publication, compacted payloads, bounded queues, relay retry/resync, browser reconnect invalidation and authorization rechecks before delivery; inspected workspace-events and relay test source.

Executed node .codex-context/runs/predeploy-review-20261014/automation/reproduce.mjs from /Users/artem/visua using SQLite :memory: and synthetic data only. Recorded five passing fixture cases in reproduce.log: overload recovery defect reproduction; successful manual retry counterevidence; SSE overflow/resync plus withholding after revocation; run epoch/cancel fencing; synthetic restricted task redaction. No external requests, services or model calls were made.

findings.mechanism: Trigger: a connector is requested while all four process-wide connector slots are occupied. withConnectorBudget refuses admission with ConnectorCapacityError before running the connector, but runConnector treats every such rejection as a connector execution failure and persists status=error. Once capacity returns, run_checks filters exclusively for status=active, including explicit connectorId requests, so subsequent Evidence Collector/Task Executor attempts never retry this healthy connector. The error then tells the user to add a connector even though it already exists.
findings.evidence: Executed reproduction in reproduce.mjs/reproduce.log: four held connector budgets caused service.runConnector to reject with ConnectorCapacityError and persist error; after releasing every held slot, runChecks.run({connectorId}) returned No active connectors and physicalRuns remained 0. Source: connectors/limits.ts:12 performs pre-execution admission refusal; visua.ts:1581-1589 persists error for it; tools.ts:757-758 excludes that state. Counterevidence: a direct/manual retry succeeds, restores active at visua.ts:1595, and physicalRuns becomes 1; EvidencePage.tsx:287-297 leaves the Run button available irrespective of connector status. This limits severity and provides a current workaround.
findings.recommendation: Keep ConnectorCapacityError as transient admission rejection without changing connector health or lastRunAt; distinguish enabled/disabled configuration from last execution health so retryable failures remain eligible for later agent runs. Add an isolated regression covering full capacity, capacity release, and a successful subsequent agent request. Until fixed, use the existing connector Run button after overload to restore agent eligibility.

limitations: This was one bounded source review with targeted synthetic fixtures, not exhaustive path or load testing. Source-only analyses of production PostgreSQL failover, process crashes, DNS rebinding, repository path races and real provider streaming were not newly reproduced.
The repository test names and bodies cited as inspected were not executed by this worker; the lead owns full pnpm check, dependency audit and shared build/test lanes.

No live tenant, external credentials, local service at port 8787, external models, production provider endpoints or container/service mutations were used. Hosted capacity and operator configuration remain outside this evidence.
The fixture uses a synthetic connector behind the actual budget and service boundary; it establishes overload classification and retry eligibility, not real remote endpoint behavior.
